rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.

CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.

claude_reviews.summary: Top observations (hypotheses/missing validation unless noted; I did not run code). (1) sportsbook.py:189-201 vs 194-205: selection and the stake use pre-cap values while evidence-adjusted probability/edge is reused; edge for stake sizing at line 201 is computed from the evidence-adjusted probability but memory_details (line 212) records p (adjusted) as 'adjusted_probability' with the base in 'baseline'; the selection key max(x[0]-threshold) is fine, but 'edge' passed to stake is the adjusted edge, so a probability blend from evidence_decisions.py:134 can raise stake sizing beyond what the 0.5-unit cap intends only if cap logic at sportsbook.py:205 is skipped (cap applies only when stake_cap is not None; threshold-only tightening caps at 1 unit via evidence_decisions.py:93). Verify no path leaves adjusted-edge stakes uncapped. (2) evidence_decisions.py:122,144 uses date-string comparison (history date < now.date()) as a temporal-leakage guard; same-day games already completed or timezone mismatches (UTC date vs local game date) could admit or wrongly reject history; also trend rows are only date-checked, not tied to the quote time. Definite-ish gap: the injury 'latest' availability check (line 117-118) requires the absent player's rows to all be 'out', but self.availability is populated only when all rows share one fetched_utc stamp (line 61-62), so a single multi-stamp file silently disables all availability holds without recording an error. (3) sportsbook.py:164-172 settlement and 156-163 references: pregame-reference INSERT OR REPLACE can overwrite a prior reference with a later-observed quote on re-run; since game_quotes is capped at tip-1us this is bounded, but the stored label is unverified.
